problem: The formula uses rank-1 projectors |λk⟩⟨λk| but the note says the sum runs over all distinct eigenvalues. For a degenerate operator these two statements cannot both hold: a rank-1 projector does not cover a whole eigenspace, so A = Σ λk|λk⟩⟨λk| over distinct λk is false.
fix: Either say the sum runs over a full orthonormal eigenbasis (one term per eigenvector, so degenerate eigenvalues repeat), or keep distinct eigenvalues and write Pk as the projector onto the whole eigenspace of λk, i.e. f(A) = Σk f(λk)Pk.

problem: The claim that the matrix series converges whenever the number series converges at every eigenvalue is only guaranteed for diagonalisable A. A defective matrix (a Jordan block) also needs the differentiated series to converge, so the rule as written can fail.
fix: Say: for a diagonalisable operator (in particular Hermitian or unitary A) f(A) exists whenever the number series converges at every eigenvalue; for defective matrices the derived series must converge too.

problem: "f(A) has the same eigenvectors as A" is not always true. If f takes the same value on two different eigenvalues of A, f(A) has extra eigenvectors; for example f(A) = I when f is constant on the spectrum.
fix: Say: f(A) is diagonal in the eigenbasis of A, so A and f(A) commute; if f is one-to-one on the spectrum, f(A) has exactly the same eigenvectors as A.

problem: The trap quotes entries 1 and e but never names the function being applied, so a student cannot tell that the example is about exp.
fix: Write: applying f(x) = eˣ entry by entry to X = [[0, 1], [1, 0]] would give [[1, e], [e, 1]], which is wrong; the correct value is cosh(1)I + sinh(1)X.
